review.note: Illustrative guidance written for the explorer from the cited sources and the CEOS-ARD fitness-for-purpose pillar. It has not been reviewed or endorsed by CEOS, the Ramsar Convention or domain experts. The need-to-family table and the detail and frequency bands are proposals for review by the relevant Virtual Constellations.

needs.label: surface water and flooding
needs.explanation: Open water shows in both optical and radar data. Radar sees through cloud; optical helps tell vegetation types apart. Both families stay in the results.

needs.label: vegetation and crop condition
needs.explanation: Vegetation condition is usually read from optical surface reflectance. Cloud limits how often you get a usable look.

needs.label: land cover and how it changes
needs.explanation: Land cover is usually mapped from optical surface reflectance. Where cloud persists, radar can fill gaps; you can add it in the filters.

needs.label: ground movement and structure
needs.explanation: Radar responds to surface roughness, structure and moisture, and interferometric products measure ground movement. It works day or night and through cloud.

needs.label: surface temperature and heat
needs.explanation: Thermal-infrared measurements expressed as land surface temperature. Cloud limits observations.

needs.label: burnt area
needs.explanation: Burnt area is usually mapped from optical surface reflectance before and after a fire.

needs.label: water colour and quality
needs.explanation: Water colour comes from Aquatic Reflectance. No CEOS-ARD assessed Aquatic Reflectance products are in this catalogue yet, so the list will be empty; that gap is shown rather than hidden.

needs.label: not sure — show me what each can do
needs.explanation: No measurement family filter is applied. The checks explain what each measurement can and cannot show.

assumptions: The catalogue lists products and their reported characteristics. It does not check acquisitions over your area or period.
CEOS-ARD assessment describes conformance with a Product Family Specification; it does not establish suitability for your purpose.

checks.label: Observations exist for your area and period
checks.why: Reported coverage and nominal revisit describe scope and opportunity, not actual usable observations over your area and dates.

checks.label: Quality indicators and uncertainty are adequate for your use
checks.why: Products should state their measurand and uncertainty and provide quality indicators so users can assess usability (CALVAL#2–3). Where evidence is not reported here, that is a gap to investigate, not a sign of poor quality.

checks.label: Suitability for your method is established
checks.why: Quality can be documented through metrics; fitness for a use needs evaluation against that use. Assessment, measured quality and your requirements are separate questions.

checks.label: Product resolution against the smallest thing you need to tell apart
checks.why: The detail band orders results by reported pixel spacing. Pixel spacing is not the size of the smallest feature you can detect, and it is not positional accuracy, so compare it with your own smallest feature.

checks.label: Usable observations when you need them
checks.why: Nominal revisit is an observation opportunity, not a count of usable, cloud-free observations or a delivery frequency. Check acquisitions over your area for the times you need.

checks.label: Production continues for the years you need
checks.why: Ongoing monitoring depends on the mission and the product continuing. Mission status and planned end dates are context, not a commitment to keep producing the product.

checks.label: The archive covers the years you need
checks.why: Observation record periods are not established in this catalogue, and mission age does not prove continuity.

checks.label: Dates can be compared consistently
checks.why: Change detection compares observations from different dates. Check geometric consistency between dates and whether processing changed during the record. CEOS-ARD assessment documents describe the geometric and radiometric processing that was assessed.

checks.label: The archive covers the years you need
checks.why: Observation record periods are not established in this catalogue, and mission age does not prove continuity.

checks.label: The record is stable enough to show real change
checks.why: Drift in a sensor, biases between replacement sensors and changes in sampling can look like change. WGClimate has proposed Goal-level stability metrics for CEOS-ARD; most products do not report them yet.

checks.label: Radiometric and geometric accuracy are reported at the level you need
checks.why: Measuring a physical quantity needs stated accuracy and uncertainty. In this catalogue most products do not report these values yet; that is a gap to check in the assessment documents, not a sign of poor quality.

checks.label: Products can be combined without hidden bias
checks.why: The draft CEOS-ARD Strategy aims for products that can be swapped or mixed in a time series or multi-mission analysis without introducing hidden biases. Check how each product was calibrated and processed before combining them.

checks.label: Reference data to check your map’s accuracy
checks.why: A map is derived from the product by classification. Its accuracy depends on your method and reference data, not only on the product.

guidance.summary: Illustrative wetlands guidance drawn from Ramsar Technical Report No. 10. It explains considerations and checks; it does not set numeric thresholds.
assumptions: Satellite products are inputs. Water and wetland maps are derived from them by classification and checking.
Small wetlands, water under vegetation and cloudy seasons are common limitations in the cited guidance.

checks.label: Usable observations in each season you need
checks.why: Seasonally and intermittently flooded areas need observations through the year; the cited report notes observation frequency can be insufficient to track wetland changes. Nominal revisit is not a count of usable observations.

checks.label: Cloud-free optical observations in your wet season
checks.why: Persistent cloud can make much optical imagery unusable in some regions.

checks.label: Whether water under vegetation must be detected
checks.why: Floating vegetation and flooding below canopies are difficult to detect with optical or C-band SAR alone; the cited report suggests L-band SAR may help. Check each product's radar band and mode in its documentation.

checks.label: Product resolution against the smallest wetland you must detect
checks.why: Small wetlands may be missed at coarser resolution. The cited report describes high-resolution data as necessary for detailed assessments; it does not set one threshold for all purposes, so the explorer does not set one for you. Pixel spacing is not the size of the smallest detectable feature.

checks.label: Reference or field data to validate your results
checks.why: The cited report stresses that in-situ data and local knowledge remain critical, and that adequate ground data is needed to validate derived maps.

family_notes.sr: Optical data help distinguish vegetation types, but persistent cloud limits usable observations in some regions and seasons.
family_notes.sar: Radar can observe through cloud and haze, which the cited report highlights for cloudy regions. Open water usually appears dark; detecting flooding beneath vegetation depends on band and conditions.
family_notes.st: The cited wetlands guidance does not discuss surface-temperature products for inundation. Check that temperature measures what you need.
family_notes.both: The cited report discusses optical and radar as complementary: optical for vegetation types, radar for observations through cloud.
family_notes.decide: For water and wetlands, the cited report discusses both optical and radar data. Comparing one of each is a reasonable way to start; the explorer does not choose for you.

use_notes.map: A water or wetland map is a derived product: classifying water and wetland types and assessing map accuracy are steps you, or a processing service, carry out. The explorer does not perform them.
use_notes.change: A series of inundation maps is a derived product: classifying water (including flooded vegetation where needed), combining dates and assessing accuracy are steps you, or a processing service, carry out. The explorer does not perform them.
